doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: The recording ban and the decline of big bands
summary: Bert explains how the ban let vocalists with strings take over from big bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What did the musicians in general think about that recording ban?

We had to go along with it, but that ruined the big band business. Because then vocalists started recording with string sections, recorded in Europe, which they could do, and all of a sudden the vocalists were the big thing.
Yeah. People’s tastes changed because that’s all they were getting?
Yeah. Before there were singers with bands, like Frank Sinatra, Peggy Lee, they were band singers. And now the band accompanied them. It reversed. So it ruined the big bands.
It’s too bad. It lasted almost two years, didn’t it?
Yeah. Then there was another one around ’47.
Oh. I didn’t know about that.
